Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **Characters straight from PSD and CLIP STUDIO PAINT files**: a character drawn from layers can take each pose from the `.psd` or `.clip` the artists draw in, with no layer structure to export (`doc/world.txt`, "The layers in a PSD or CLIP STUDIO PAINT file"). `psd://name.psd/...` loads a Photoshop layer as `clip://` does
- **kagex-release splits PSD and CLIP files into layer pictures**: a release carries each file's layer structure and a TLG picture per layer instead of the file, so it's smaller and plays on the web, Android and iOS, which have no plugins to read the files. `kagex-release --cli split` shows what a build makes of one file
- **Mouths by vowel**: a mouth group with a layer for each vowel shows the vowel the voice says, from the voice's lip track (`<voice>.lip`). A voice without one opens and shuts the mouth by how loud it is, as before
- **kagex-lipsync**, a new tool beside kagex-release (`tools/` in the Windows and Linux packages, and a download of its own): pick the voices that should shape their characters' mouths to the vowels, and it writes their lip tracks from each voice and its line in the scripts, by forced alignment with PocketSphinx and OpenJTalk (Japanese lines, kanji included). In a game in more than one language it uses the line in the language the voice speaks. It needs its `lipsync/` folder (the speech models and the dictionary, 112 MB) beside it
- The Animated Character demo's Pip says one line in a synthesized voice to show the vowels; its other lines are babble and move the mouth by loudness
- Lip-sync without a track keeps in time with the voice more often: the engine sometimes reads a voice's level half a second ahead, which the mouth now works around
- kagex-release 0.11.0 downloads the 0.11.0 engines

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.11.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
